layers.authority: Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India (e-FRRO portal)
layers.process: The entire area of Arunachal Pradesh is a Protected Area (Third Schedule, Immigration and Foreigners Order 2025). Every foreigner needs a Protected Area Permit. Apply online at indianfrro.gov.in (e-FRRO) or the Indian Visa Su-Swagatam app; permits are electronic only. Indian missions advise getting approval 30 days ahead if applying with the visa, or 15 days ahead via the FRRO if already in India.

layers.authority: Department of Tourism, Government of Arunachal Pradesh
layers.process: Foreign tourists pay a royalty of USD 30 per head to the Government of Arunachal Pradesh, and tourist PAP applications go through an approved local tour operator only.

laws.rule: The whole of Arunachal Pradesh is a Protected Area: a foreigner must hold a permit to enter or stay. The civil authority can attach conditions, including reporting to police and limits on surveying, sketching or photography.

Tourist eILP (Indian citizens only): valid for stays up to 14 days; ₹300 (about A$4.47 at the RBA rate of 30 October 2026) up to 3 days, ₹500 for 4 to 14 days. Under-14s need no eILP if with an adult. Foreign nationals apply for a PAP/RAP via e-FRRO.
